rusutsu-snow-drift.hook: Slide a 4WD Subaru sideways across a snowed-in golf course.
moments: Check in at the Rusutsu Resort Hotel Activity Desk, blow into the breathalyzer, then ride the shuttle 15 minutes to the course.
Step out onto the Riverwood golf course, now a white track of packed snow and snow banks.
Hold on in a GT-R or GR Yaris while the instructor throws it sideways, snow spraying past the window.
Drive a Subaru B4 or automatic Impreza yourself, and feel the rear step out as the instructor calls the steering.
Film the ride from the passenger seat; filming is allowed, so bring a phone mount or chest strap.
rusutsu-snow-drift.tip: Book by 17:00 the day before. Take the 8:30 slot for fresh, even snow. Wear warm shoes you can feel pedals in; rental shoes exist.

initial-d-haruna-day.hook: Drive Takumi's real tofu run down 'Akina' to Lake Haruna.
moments: Stand at the Yaseone old toll gate by the water tower, the start line of the Akina downhill races.
Drive the tight hairpins slowly and look at the gutters, where Takumi does his famous gutter-drop move.
Walk to frozen-edged Lake Haruna and see the Mt Haruna cone reflected across the water.
Look at the Fujiwara Tofu Shop storefront and AE86 displays in the Ikaho car museum.
Climb the 365 Ikaho stone steps and eat hot yu-no-hana manju, the same buns from the anime.
initial-d-haruna-day.tip: Go on a clear, dry day and drive the pass before noon, before shade ice forms. The road surface is rough, so go slow.

irohazaka-nikko-bus.hook: Ride a normal city bus up 48 hairpins, each one marked with a letter.
moments: Sit at the front of the bus from Nikko station and count the hiragana signs: い, ろ, は, one per hairpin.
Climb 440 m on the uphill Second Irohazaka, the road where team Emperor's Evos race in Initial D Third Stage.
Stand at Kegon Falls, a 97 m drop that is often partly frozen into ice columns in January.
Walk the snowy approach to Toshogu shrine and find the carved Sleeping Cat and three wise monkeys.
Ride back down the separate one-way First Irohazaka, with its 28 downhill curves.
irohazaka-nikko-bus.tip: Sit on the left front seat going up for the best hairpin view. Check if the Akechidaira ropeway runs in winter before you plan it.

megamiko-ice-driving.hook: Learn to steer with the throttle on a frozen lake 1,540 m up.
moments: Arrive at 07:00 as the gate opens, with the lake white and flat, and the cold biting through your gloves.
Weave a pylon slalom in the orange area, feeling the car start to slide at just 20 km/h.
Hold a steady circle and figure eight in the green area until the slide feels natural.
Warm up with the included lunch and free drinks around 11:00.
Run the 500 m ice circuit in the blue area and link the corners in long slides.
megamiko-ice-driving.tip: Most events need your own car on studless tyres. Ask Fun2Drive in Hakone early if their rental-car ice event runs again in 2027.

ebisu-drift-taxi.hook: A D1 champion drifts you around Ebisu in a Mark II taxi.
moments: Buckle into the bucket seats of the drift taxi, a Toyota Mark II JZX110.
Ride with Nobushige Kumakubo, D1GP champion in 2006 and 2011, or KANTA, 2023 Formula Drift Japan champion.
Hear the tyres scream and smell the rubber smoke as the car links corners at full lock.
Watch practice cars on the other Ebisu courses from the hillside after your ride.
ebisu-drift-taxi.tip: Not possible on this trip: closed Dec 20 to Mar 31, and paused since 2025. Keep it for a spring or autumn visit.

tokyo-drift-day-tour.hook: Pick your JDM hero car, from R34 to Nismo GT-R, and drift it.
moments: Get picked up at your hotel at 07:00 and listen to the safety briefing on the drive out.
Choose your car: R34 Skyline, Supra MK4, RX-7 FD, Integra Type R, WRX STI S202, or an R35 GT-R.
Drive three hours of drift sessions from 09:00 with an instructor beside you, first slow circles, then linked slides.
Eat the included lunch at 12:00, then do two more hours of sessions in the afternoon.
Ride passenger with the instructor to feel a full-speed drift before you head back.
tokyo-drift-day-tour.tip: Only drivers aged 26+ with an IDP can drive. Ask which circuit they use in January before paying the ¥100,000 deposit.

fuji-motorsports-museum.hook: See the Le Mans-winning Mazda 787B next to Fuji Speedway.
moments: Start with the oldest cars: an 1899 Panhard et Levassor and the 1902 Ford 999.
Stand in front of the 1965 Honda RA272, the first Japanese car to win an F1 race.
Look at the orange and green 1991 Mazda 787B, the first Japanese Le Mans overall winner.
Find the rally cars: Subaru Impreza 555 and Mitsubishi Lancer 1600GSR, then the HKS GR Supra drift car.
Step outside to see the long Fuji Speedway straight with snowy Mt Fuji behind it.
fuji-motorsports-museum.tip: Book online a month ahead for ¥1,600. Exhibits rotate, so check the site's exhibit list before you go.

nissan-heritage-zama.hook: Walk rows of 300 Nissans, and hear some of them start.
moments: Walk into the long hall inside Nissan's Zama plant with about 300 cars in rows.
Find the 1969 'Hakosuka' Skyline GT-R and the S30 Fairlady Z from the same year.
See the Group A Skyline race cars and the R390 GT1 Le Mans car.
Listen as the guide starts the engines of some cars on weekdays; about 70% still run.
Look back at 1930s Datsuns and 1950s–60s Prince Skylines to see where the GT-R started.
nissan-heritage-zama.tip: Apply online about a month ahead and pick a weekday slot, because weekday tours sometimes include engine starts. Entry is free.

tokyo-bay-pa-night.hook: Sit in a JDM meet under the city lights, then drive under the sea.
moments: Pull into Tatsumi PA, a small parking area on the expressway with the city skyline right behind the parked cars.
Walk the rows and look for tuned Skylines, Silvias and RX-7s, but do not touch the cars.
Drive into the 9.6 km Aqualine tunnel that runs under Tokyo Bay.
Come up at Umihotaru, a rest stop island in the bay, and walk the open deck in the cold sea wind.
See the lights of the bay, and on clear nights Mt Fuji in the distance.
tokyo-bay-pa-night.tip: Friday or Saturday nights get the most cars. The Aqualine toll is about ¥3,140 by cash. Police may close Tatsumi when it gets busy.

nissan-crossing-ginza.hook: Free Nissan showroom on the most famous corner in Ginza.
moments: Walk into Ginza Place at the Ginza 4-chome crossing and see the display cars under bright white lights.
Look at the new and special Nissan models, which change during the year.
Go up to the café and order a drink while you look down at the Ginza crossing.
Buy Nissan and GT-R goods in the shop before you leave.
nissan-crossing-ginza.tip: Go after dark, when the Wako clock tower and Ginza lights are on outside. Check the site for the cars on show in January.

honda-collection-hall-motegi.hook: Honda keeps about 350 machines here, and all of them still run.
moments: Start at the Honda Dream A from 1947, the first product with the Honda name.
See the T360 mini truck from 1963, Honda's first four-wheeler.
Stand at the white and red RA272, Honda's first F1 winner in 1965.
Look at the NR500 race bike with its strange oval pistons.
Watch a scheduled engine start-up demo, then meet the ASIMO robots.
honda-collection-hall-motegi.tip: Check the Motegi calendar first: the hall has winter closure days. Use the free smartphone audio guide and bring earphones.

tokyo-auto-salon-2027.hook: Asia's biggest tuning show fills eleven halls near Narita.
moments: Get to Makuhari Messe before 09:00 and go straight to the booths with new car reveals.
Walk Halls 1 to 11 past widebody builds, tuned GT-Rs and Supras, and maker booths like GR and NISMO.
Go outside to the demo area and watch drift runs, with engine noise and tyre smoke in the cold air.
Look for pro drivers signing autographs at the maker booths.
Buy tuner stickers, keychains and shirts in the goods area before the crowds peak.
tokyo-auto-salon-2027.tip: Buy digital tickets in advance only. Saturday gets the most people; enter at opening and see the biggest booths first.

up-garage-sapporo.hook: Dig through used JDM parts bins for cheap car souvenirs.
moments: Walk rows of used wheels stacked by size and brand.
Look through the steering wheels, shift knobs and gauges in the small parts shelves.
Find old badges, mirror parts or a shift knob that fits in your suitcase.
Compare prices on the tags; used parts here are often far cheaper than new.
up-garage-sapporo.tip: Check the store's stock and hours online before you take a taxi out. Check your home country's customs rules for car parts.

toyota-automobile-museum.hook: About 150 cars from all makers, with the Toyota 2000GT as the star.
moments: Ride the Linimo maglev line to Geidai-dori station and walk to the museum.
Walk the Car Hall, from early European cars to Japanese cars, about 150 in total.
Stand at the white Toyota 2000GT, Japan's classic 1960s sports car.
See the special show on Japan's motorization, open until Feb 28, 2027.
Eat in the museum restaurant or café before you leave.
toyota-automobile-museum.tip: Closed Mondays. Arrive at 09:30 opening for empty halls. Only worth it if you fly in or out of Nagoya.
